title: Collect rainwater for garden irrigation
summary: Treat roof runoff as non-potable water; prefer verified safe water for edible crops and follow current local health guidance.
content: Treat roof runoff as non-potable water; prefer verified safe water for edible crops and follow current local health guidance. Use the steps as a conservative offline checklist, then follow current local rules, official alerts, product labels and competent agricultural or food-safety advice.
materials: clean dedicated containers or tools appropriate to the task
steps: Check local rules, roof materials, gutters and the previous use of every tank or barrel before collection.
Fit a secure cover and screened openings so children, animals, debris and mosquitoes cannot enter.
Divert the dirtiest initial roof runoff where practical and keep fuel, pesticide, lead-painted or chemically treated surfaces out of the collection path.
Prefer public-system or otherwise verified safe water for edible crops. If current local guidance permits collected rainwater, apply it at soil level and avoid splashing edible parts.
Inspect after storms for odour, algae, sediment, leaks and mosquito breeding; clean and isolate questionable water.
warnings: Rainwater is not automatically safe. CDC advises using public-system tap water or bottled water, when possible, for watering plants you plan to eat.
Never connect a rain barrel directly to drinking-water plumbing or allow backflow into it.
common_mistakes: Scaling up before a small controlled trial.
Using an unidentified material, water source, seed lot or crop.
Ignoring weather, local rules, product labels or signs of contamination.
alternatives: Reduce the plan to one small test batch or container.
Use a safer established water, seed, crop or food method when any critical condition is uncertain.
failure_signs: Unexpected odour, slime, mould, contamination, structural movement, uncontrolled pests, crop collapse or results that contradict the verified method.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this guide to override an emergency order, food recall, pesticide label, building restriction, water restriction or professional diagnosis.
short_term: Protect people, drinking water and uncontaminated food first; isolate the uncertain material and record what happened.
long_term: Keep a seasonal record of materials, varieties, water, weather, yields, losses and corrections.
if_method_fails: Stop scaling up, isolate the problem and return to a verified small trial or qualified local advice.
environment_notes: Adapt for Mediterranean heat, wind, drought, local frost, balcony exposure and the actual microclimate.
